# Requirements Checklist: Split chat pane

**Purpose**: Validate that `specs/005-split-chat-pane/spec.md` is testable, unambiguous, free of
implementation detail in its requirements, and internally consistent before `/speckit.plan`
design is trusted.
**Created**: 2026-10-02
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature
context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact.
Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is
satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements
quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the maximum number of simultaneous panes stated as a hard limit, not left open?
      [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK002 Is what each pane must show enumerated completely (header, transcript, message box,
      queue, approvals/questions, future readout row), rather than left to "the usual chat UI"?
      [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK003 Are both ways of starting a split (row-menu item and Ctrl+click) specified with the
      same resulting behaviour, so neither is an afterthought? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK004 Is the behaviour of every control a pane contains (message box, Stop, queue chips,
      approval/question controls) scoped to "its own session only"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK005 Is restart behaviour specified for all three session outcomes (both exist, one
      archived/missing, neither exists would collapse to zero panes) rather than only the happy
      path? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, §FR-015, US4/AC3]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "focused pane" defined precisely enough (exactly one at a time, marked by more
      than colour, set by click/type/keyboard) that two engineers would build the same thing?
      [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006]
- [x] CHK007 Is the keyboard-only focus-move requirement clear that its exact chord is
      intentionally deferred, rather than silently missing? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK008 Is "replace" (the effect of a row click or Open in split on the target pane)
      distinguished clearly from "add a third pane" and from "focus the other pane", with each
      case given its own requirement? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009, §FR-012]
- [x] CHK009 Is the minimum-pane-width collapse behaviour described in concrete, testable terms
      (one pane shown, second session one action away, re-splits automatically) rather than a
      vague "responsive" statement? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Do FR-014/FR-015 (restart restores a split only when both sessions exist and are not
      archived) agree with Edge Cases and US4/AC3 on what happens to a dropped session? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK011 Do FR-009 (never show the same session in both panes) and the Edge Cases entry
      ("The same session is never shown in both panes at once") state the same rule without
      contradiction? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK012 Does FR-018's unread rule for a split pane match spec 001 FR-006's single-pane rule
      exactly (viewed while focused-window, unread otherwise), rather than inventing a new rule?
      [Consistency, Spec §FR-018, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK013 Do FR-003/FR-020 (readout chip row, Subagents panel) and the Assumptions section
      agree that both are no-ops until spec 004 ships, with no contradicting requirement elsewhere
      that assumes spec 004 already exists? [Consistency]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK014 Does every user story's acceptance scenario set use a testable Given/When/Then shape
      with one observable outcome per scenario? [Acceptance Criteria Quality, Spec §US1-US4]
- [x] CHK015 Can SC-001 to SC-007 each be verified by an external observer (timing, counting,
      presence/absence) without reading the implementation? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK016 Does SC-004 ("same session never shown in both panes... across every way of opening
      or changing a pane") actually enumerate "every way" via FR-001/FR-008/FR-009/FR-012, so the
      claim is checkable rather than aspirational? [Acceptance Criteria Quality, Spec §SC-004]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK017 Is the "put a second session beside the first" scenario covered from both entry
      points (row menu and Ctrl+click) and for both the already-open and newly-chosen session?
      [Coverage, Spec §US1]
- [x] CHK018 Is the keyboard-only path (no pointer) covered for every interactive element the
      split introduces: opening, focus-move, divider resize, pane close? [Coverage, Spec §US1/AC4,
      §US2/AC3, §FR-023]
- [x] CHK019 Is the "closing back down to one pane" path covered for both panes (closing either
      one, not just one specific side)? [Coverage, Spec §US3/AC1, §US3/AC3]
- [x] CHK020 Is a concurrent-streaming scenario (both panes' turns running at once, neither
      delayed) present and distinct from the single-session streaming scenarios inherited from
      spec 001? [Coverage, Spec §US1/AC6, §SC-002]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK021 Is the archived/deleted/agent-stopped pane behaviour specified per cause (archived,
      deleted, agent stopped) rather than lumped into one vague "error state"? [Edge Case Coverage,
      Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK022 Is the narrow-window edge case specified with both directions (narrowing collapses,
      widening re-splits automatically)? [Edge Case Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-017]
- [x] CHK023 Is the cold-starting-session-in-a-pane case addressed so it is not confused with an
      error state? [Edge Case Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK024 Is the case of a pane's repository being removed from Refract addressed, instead of
      being left as an unstated crash risk? [Edge Case Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK025 Is the interaction between the split and the Settings/Pull-requests views (which
      replace the chat area) addressed, so the split's persistence rule doesn't conflict with a
      view switch? [Edge Case Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-021]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK026 Are accessibility requirements for the split stated explicitly (labelled regions,
      focus-change announcements, full keyboard operability, visible focus indicator), not left
      implicit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022, §FR-023, §SC-005]
- [x] CHK027 Is the "no observable delay" performance requirement between panes stated as a
      measurable non-functional requirement rather than a vague "stays responsive"? [Measurability,
      Spec §FR-004, §SC-002]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK028 Are this spec's dependencies on spec 001 (US5, FR-006, FR-018, FR-019, FR-049) named
      explicitly rather than assumed implicitly? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK029 Are the two genuinely open readings (narrow-window collapse behaviour; replacing the
      unfocused pane in the one case Stuart was not directly asked about) labelled as unconfirmed
      assumptions rather than presented as settled decisions? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK030 Is the dependency on spec 004 (readout chip row, Subagents panel) scoped so this
      spec's own requirements remain independently buildable before spec 004 ships? [Dependency,
      Spec §Assumptions]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK031 Is there any requirement that assumes more than two panes, conflicting with
      FR-002's two-pane cap? None found. [Conflict, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK032 Is there any requirement that assumes a stacked (top/bottom) layout, conflicting with
      the side-by-side-only Assumption? None found. [Conflict, Spec §Assumptions]

## Traceability

- [x] CHK033 Does every functional requirement (FR-001 to FR-023) map to at least one user story
      or edge case in this spec? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements]
- [x] CHK034 Does every success criterion (SC-001 to SC-007) map to at least one functional
      requirement it measures? [Traceability, Spec §Success Criteria]
